also: it looks that way to me

terms.gloss: seem, appear (to be or to do)
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation: the passive of videō, with a nominative and infinitive
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.83: ut imbellēs timidīque videāmur
terms.comment: Latin makes the person or thing the subject: vidēris fessus esse, “you seem tired”. The impersonal vidētur with an accusative and infinitive is rare (Lewis & Short). Ut vidētur, as it seems (Traupman 27).

terms.gloss: it seems to me, I think
terms.grammar: phrase: the person in the dative
evidence: Cic. Lael. 27: ā nātūrā mihi vidētur potius quam ab indigentiā orta amīcitia (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With sī, the polite form of a suggestion: sī tibi vidētur, if you agree.

phrases.latin: nōn semper ea sunt quae videntur
phrases.english: things are not always what they seem
do I seem angry to you now?

phrases.latin: quia videor ācer, alligant mē interdiū
phrases.english: because I seem fierce, they tie me up by day

phrases.latin: aliquid natābat quod prīmō aspectū alga ipsa vidēbātur
phrases.english: something was swimming that at first sight seemed to be the seaweed itself
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium
